title: Vouchers for public school students cited

blocks.text: Elementary students in General Trias, Cavite line up during flag ceremony in this file photo from June of this year.

MANILA, Philippines — Senators welcomed the enactment of Republic Act 12327, or the Basic Education Voucher Assistance Act, which allows students from overcrowded public schools to enroll in private schools using government-funded vouchers.

Signed by President Marcos on Nov. 12 and released on Friday, the law institutionalizes a portable, learner-held voucher system – allowing families to choose government-recognized private schools rather than tying subsidies to school-allocated slots under existing programs.

Priority is given to low-income households, including 4Ps beneficiaries, while persons with disabilities, orphans, indigenous peoples and learners in geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas automatically qualify.
Sen. Francis Pangilinan, a co-author of the consolidated Senate measure, stressed that the voucher program must complement – and not replace – state investments in public school infrastructure.
Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano, whose bill was consolidated into the law, said the measure could help ease congestion and bring out-of-school children back to classrooms amid declining enrollment.
